mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5.25% for two consecutive months, investors anticipate prolonged higher policy rates, which reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the horizon are positive and statistically significant (t-test p < 0.05) despite the high-rate condition, or the policy rate drops below 5.25% within 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, prompting equity risk-on positioning and positive 20-day forward S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% month-over-month AND UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not statistically significant (Rank IC > 0.05) or forward returns are negative despite the labor signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months predicts increased corporate demand for equity financing, leading to positive 5-day forward S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > INDPRO_12MA for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Five-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) or INDPRO does not sustain the expansion signal.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2.0% for two months suggests the Federal Reserve is likely to hold rates steady, reducing discount rate expectations and producing negative 20-day forward S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant despite the low inflation signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds +2.5% in a month, it indicates accelerating inflation, prompting preemptive rate hikes and a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) despite the inflation signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% followed by a sustained rise in job openings (HOUST) suggests a tight labor market, which elevates equity risk-on sentiment and produces positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5 AND HOUST increases by >5% month-over-month
failure_condition: Interaction effect is not significant (Rank IC > 0.05) or forward returns are not positive in this regime.

mechanism_narrative: A two consecutive months of declining retail sales (PAYEMS) accompanied by rising industrial production (INDPRO) suggests sector rotation toward manufacturing, which is associated with positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases for two consecutive months AND INDPRO increases for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or not statistically significant despite the rotation signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of real GDP deflator (not directly observable here; fallback: a proxy such as the 12-month change in INDPRO normalized by CPIAUCSL) turns negative, it indicates deflationary pressures, reducing discount rate expectations and producing negative 5-day forward returns.
regime_hint: Deflationary pressure detected via supply-side indicators
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant despite the deflationary signal.
